title: Dead or Alive 3 (USA) (En,Ja).xiso.iso
prediction:
defer_cap 15 -> 12 IN UNLOCK MODE. One constant. Arm A 9931f882bb (cap 15, the shipped value), arm B 2e4e8403d9 (cap 12), differing by that line plus its comment and a regenerated symbol index. DOA3, 240 s, --device thor, one --who, TWO runs per arm as separate soaks. device_label read out of all four result.json files. Judge docs/testing/vblank_defercap_ab.py, with docs/testing/vblank_roundtrip.py for the round-trip figures.

WHY TWELVE, AND THE REASON IS NOT THE ONE D9 GAVE. #65's D9 failed: cap 15's worst fully-unlocked window still clamps 5 times against a bar of 2, diagnosed as `def_max - max_defer` reaching 3,083,365 ns so that one poll interval of margin does not cover the timer round trip. The value 12 was then argued as "4,170,938 ns, 1.35x the observed maximum". THAT ARGUMENT IS REFUTED, and by data already on disk rather than by this arm: 3,083,365 ns is a maximum over the ~32 fully-unlocked windows those two runs happened to contain, and the same estimator regime-conditioned over the ~110 usable windows of each of those SAME runs reaches 3,691,090 to 6,534,801 ns. Twelve's margin is 0.64x the observed maximum, not 1.35x. The tail was under-sampled, which is this campaign's own "a within-ref floor is a lower bound on the floor, never the floor".

Twelve survives for a different and better reason -- the occupancy-free window count, over the four thor soaks of #65's own arms:

    windows holding a deferral whose round trip exceeds the margin
      cap 15   37  25  28  28    <- what shipped
      cap 14   17  14  18  16
      cap 13    8   5   1   3
      cap 12    0   0   0   1    <- eliminated
      cap 11    0   0   0   1

Twelve is the KNEE. Eleven buys nothing, and the single residual window is the 6.53 ms event the maximum-based argument had mispriced. So the claim under test is "the exceedance count reaches zero", not "the margin covers the maximum".

E0 (GATE, and the pair is VOID without it): each arm has at least 5 fully-unlocked windows. #65's arms gave 34, 6, 20, 12. A cap that only exists in unlock mode cannot be tested by a soak that never enters it -- which is exactly why this is the thor on DOA3 and not the nova on anything.

E1 (THE MECHANISM, in the one form that does not move with occupancy): arm B has ZERO fully-unlocked windows whose `def(max=) - max_defer` exceeds the margin the cap leaves, on BOTH runs. At cap 12 max_defer is 12,512,808 ns and the margin is 4,170,942, so the condition is `def(max=) <= 16,683,750` -- no deferral more than a period late, i.e. the clamp cannot fire FROM A DEFERRAL at all. Arm A must be non-zero for the leg to discriminate; predicted 25-37 per run from the table above. FAILS on any non-zero arm-B window.

E2 (D9's OWN BAR, re-run at the new value): arm B's worst fully-unlocked window clamps at most 2 times. This is the leg that failed at 5 with cap 15. A residual is expected and permitted here because no cap bounds a HOST STALL -- the nova's phase tail reaches 686,863,907 ns, 41x a period -- which is why the bar is 2 and not 0. FAILS at 3 or more.

E3 (GUEST TIME, absolute and not a ratio to arm A, because arm A's own clamp rate moved 3.2x between two runs of one binary and a ratio inside that noise floor cannot discriminate -- that is how D1, D5 and D7 all failed): arm B's worst run loses at most 0.40 s/min in fully-unlocked windows. Cap 15 measured 0.449 and 0.797; cap 16 measured 3.936 and 11.005. FAILS above 0.40.

E4 (THE INTERMEDIATE VALUE, which is the half of this prediction that can fail on a working change): the deferred hold in fully-unlocked windows falls by 3,128,202 ns -- exactly three poll intervals, because 15 -> 12 is three -- RUN-PAIRED, within +-20%. This is the constant read off the device rather than inferred from the source, and it is registered as a value rather than a direction: a change that "merely helped" would not land on three poll intervals. Cross-paired it may fail, because arm A's own hold moved 1,227,019 ns between runs, and that is recorded as a DIAGNOSIS rather than counted -- D5's cross-paired failure at cap 15 was exactly this and the run-paired figures were 5.4% and 7.2% off one poll interval, i.e. the constant measured twice.

E5 (THE COST, and it is the leg named in advance as most likely to fail): gfps p90 and gfps max each fall by at most 2, worst run of each arm. THIS IS NOT FREE BY PRECEDENT. The 15 step removed 6.25% of the deferral's headroom and cost nothing measurable (p90 59 -> 59, max 59 -> 59); this one removes 25%. Three arms in a row have now failed to show the deferral's frame-rate defence -- #65's B4, its U6, and D6 -- but a 4x larger cut has no precedent, and the deferral exists precisely to give a late frame room to finish. FAILS at a fall of 3 or more, and then the entry point is still right and the value is 13, which the table above shows still removes most of the exceedance (8, 5, 1, 3 against 37, 25, 28, 28).

E6 (WITHIN-RUN CONTROL, must-not-move): the locked-window mean interval moves by at most 50,000 ns between arms. `defer_cap` for the locked branch is 4 and untouched, so locked mode cannot move; #65's arms moved it 1,465 ns (0.009%) and 5,735 ns (0.034%) against effects of 21% and 6%. FAILS above 50,000 ns, and then the change is reaching a regime it has no business in.

E7 (THE IMPOSSIBLE ROW): neg == 0 across every vblphase window of all four runs. A QEMU timer fires at or after its deadline and never before, so an assertion cannot precede its own grid slot. It has read 0 over 33,840 assertions across two devices, two titles and three binaries. A non-zero is an instrument fault and voids the run rather than being a finding.

E8 (THE NOVA, registered so a nova-side tail can refute this value, and ALREADY MEASURED rather than left as a hope). The nova's round trip is about twice the thor's: rt_max 6,225,835 to 50,353,011 ns and rt_p90 4,776,972 to 5,768,336 across five soaks, against the thor's rt_max 3,691,090 to 6,534,801 and rt_p90 2,423,885 to 2,844,532. At cap 12 the nova retains 12 to 29 exceedance windows of ~120 where the thor retains 0 to 1; it would need cap 10 to reach the thor's post-change level and cap 9 to approach zero. THIS IS NOT TESTABLE ON THE DEVICE TODAY and is therefore recorded as a residual and NOT counted as a leg: the nova has never entered unlock mode on any title on hand -- unl == 0 on every window of all five of those soaks -- so the constant is dead code there, and the figures above are the HOST's round trip read out of LOCKED-mode deferrals and transplanted into the unlock arithmetic. The falsifier, stated for whoever finds such a title: if a title is ever found that puts the nova in unlock mode, this predicts its cap-bound window count will NOT reach zero at 12. Shipping 10 pre-emptively would spend two further steps of a real title's deferral headroom against a configuration never observed, which is a trade for the owner and not for this lane.
must_not_move: locked-window mean interval within 50,000 ns between arms
gfps p90 falls by at most 2 (worst run of each arm)
gfps max falls by at most 2 (worst run of each arm)
neg == 0 on every vblphase window of all four runs
device_label == thor on all four results
note_refs: a_ref 9931f882bb and b_ref 2e4e8403d9 differ by `int defer_cap = unlocked ? 15 : 4;` -> `? 12 : 4`, its surrounding comment, and docs/testing/nv2a_index.json (a symbol map, no effect on the binary). Verified with `git diff 9931f882bb 2e4e8403d9`. poll_interval is deliberately NOT changed, so this remains one constant and the retry granularity is identical.
